speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they tend to worsen as the day progresses?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. Do you experience any difficulty with swallowing, chewing, or changes in your speech, particularly towards the end of the day?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness or double vision improve after you take a short rest, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids? I would also like to check for any muscle atrophy or fasciculations in your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the symptoms started a month ago, but I specifically asked if the weakness improves with rest and if you have eyelid drooping. Can you confirm if your eyelids droop and if resting helps the weakness, as this is crucial for my assessment? I will also proceed to order some diagnostic tests. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody_Request REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation_Test

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation_Test: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and the decreased muscle response on repetitive nerve stimulation, combined with your symptoms of ptosis and fatigable weakness, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
